newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans tumble to four-month low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans tumble to four-month low.

text.p: The CBOT nearby July soybean contract collapsed late and broke below $8.00 per bushel where sell stops drove the contract to its four-month low, traders said.
"The crop's getting bigger and the export sales were light this morning, especially old crop beans," a trader said.
The session low for July was $7.98, near the four-month low of $7.95-1/4 which was notched on March 3.

Broad-based long liquidation before first notice day Monday for deliveries on that contract left a near dearth of buying interest. There have been rumors a commercial firm Monday may post soybeans for delivery on the July.
Traders said Rosenthal Collins also was a steady seller of the November contract in late dealings.
"Rosenthal is just selling 500 (500,000 bushels) at a steady clip," the trader said.
At 1211 CDT, soybeans were six to 17-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 17-3/4 at $7.99. November was down nine at $6.48.
